flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -88.5% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative, so no multiple can be stated: the price assumes cash generation improves from here.

reference_note: Upper band Rs 700. At Rs 700: market cap Rs 4,009.75 cr, P/E 78.8x FY26 diluted EPS Rs 8.88, P/B 7.25x, EV/EBITDA 39.1x FY26. Institutions bought from CEAQ at Rs 700 on 29-30 Sep 2026 (pp. 151-152).
headline: A leading Indian thermal-imaging OEM that owns its technology, priced at 78.8x FY26 earnings against an 85.6x peer median; our Neutral fair value is Rs 515 (-26% vs Rs 700) because FY26 was a down year with cash tied up in orders, and the outcome turns on how quickly the Rs 432 cr of orders convert.
red_flags: Owns 100% of its IP; largest supplier of thermal imaging to Indian government agencies Apr-24 to Mar-26 (issuer-paid F&S report, pp. 246, 253)
EBITDA margin 26.2% / 29.7% / 28.9% FY24-26 and cash tax 23.3% of PBT (pp. 89, 144)
Orders of Rs 432 cr in hand (Rs 314 cr book at Jun-26 plus Rs 118 cr won Jul-Sep), about 1.2x FY26 revenue (p. 250)

FY26 revenue -22.7% as export orders slipped; reported P/E 78.8x is flattered by a Rs 18.84 cr warranty write-back and Rs 34.17 cr of capitalised development (adjusted FY26 P/E 247.5x; three-year average 75.6x) (pp. 23, 351, 373)
Priced at 78.8x FY26 EPS and 7.2x book vs peer medians 85.6x and 13.0x (pp. 141, our computation)
Fair value Rs 486 / 515 / 556 (Bear / Neutral / Bull) vs Rs 700; QIB book 293.6x at close (NSE)

anchor.mf_share: 21.05 lakh shares (57.7%) to 12 domestic mutual fund schemes
anchor.source: Anchor size: NSE issue data (121.74 lakh offered less 85.26 lakh to the public). Investor count and MF split: press reports (5paisa, inc42, hdfcsky; unverified) - the NSE anchor allocation file could not be fetched from the cloud container.

strengths: 100% ownership of IP since Mar-2024 across optics, IR engines and video processing (pp. 138, 246)
Largest supplier of thermal imaging systems to Indian government agencies Apr-24 to Mar-26; 94% of Indian thermal-imaging exports by units FY24-26 (issuer-paid F&S report, p. 246)
28,000+ systems deployed in 24 countries; ITAR-free portfolio (p. 246)
Cash tax 23.3% of cumulative FY24-26 PBT; no auditor qualifications or auditor change (pp. 89, 100, 440)
weaknesses: FY26 revenue Rs 362.65 cr, down 22.69%, as export orders slipped; Q1 FY27 is seasonally small (Rs 36.01 cr) (pp. 23, 89)
Working capital 109.7% of FY26 revenue; cumulative CFO -Rs 121.00 cr FY24-26 (pp. 87, 90)
Top-10 customers 77.83% of FY26 revenue, typical of defence tendering (p. 24)
Materials from related party CEAQ Singapore 26.3% of FY26 expenses (p. 94)
Inventory Rs 319.63 cr at Jun-26 built ahead of FY27 deliveries (pp. 25, 87)
opportunities: India EO/IR market $522 m (CY2020) to $1.4 bn (CY2030), 10.5% CAGR - issuer-paid F&S report (p. 205)
Orders of Rs 118.15 cr received Jul-Sep 2026, incl. a Rs 51.44 cr export order deferred from FY26 (pp. 23, 250)
Platform systems grew from Rs 12.70 cr (FY24) to Rs 144.81 cr (FY26) (p. 248)
IDDM eligibility under DAP 2020 favours indigenous OEMs (p. 247)
threats: Tender-based, non-recurring contracts; bid-win ratio 14.29% in Q1 FY27 vs 40.91% in FY24 (p. 23)
Export orders exposed to conflicts and export approvals: foreign-government revenue Rs 267.69 cr -> Rs 12.11 cr FY25-26 (p. 251)
Singapore High Court suit by a CEAQ Singapore minority shareholder naming the company, MD and a nominee director (p. 448)
Lock-in expiries: 287 lakh pre-issue shares (50% of capital) free after six months (p. 121)
